correctness.rationale: In coordinates \(a=(1,0)\), \(b=(c,s)\), applying one sweep to \(a^\perp\) gives squared norm \(c^2+s^2(\omega-1)^2\), proving the unique one-sweep optimum \(\omega=1\). Direct trace, determinant, and discriminant calculation gives the classical spectral-radius optimizer \(\omega_\star=2/(1+s)\) and a repeated eigenvalue \(q=(1-s)/(1+s)\). At that parameter \(T=qI+N\) with \(N^2=0\), so \(T^k=q^k(I+kN/q)\); determinant one and the Frobenius norm determine the displayed largest singular value exactly. The unrelaxed matrix is rank one with \(T_1^k=c^{2k-2}T_1\). Taylor expansion of the exact log-ratio with \(k\sqrt{s}\to\alpha\) gives coefficient \(\alpha(1-4\alpha^2/3)\). The bundled symbolic checker verifies every algebraic identity and exact rational power-norm replays; independent direct matrix calculations at multiple \(s,k\) values matched the formulas.

originality.rationale: The asymptotically optimal two-cyclic SOR/Kaczmarz relaxation is classical, and modern sources analyze relaxed Kaczmarz convergence rates. The audited contribution begins where that asymptotic statement stops: the optimizer lands at a defective double root, producing an exact polynomial transient in the Euclidean power norm, a strict one-sweep disadvantage, and an \(s^{-1/2}\) finite-horizon crossover with a sharp scaled threshold. Targeted Resultary and literature searches found no source stating or implying that complete finite-horizon profile.

value.rationale: The result exposes a concrete and practically meaningful separation between asymptotic rate tuning and finite-horizon worst-case performance in the smallest nontrivial Kaczmarz system. The exact Jordan transient, strict one-sweep cost, and crossover law quantify when the classical asymptotic optimizer becomes advantageous, making the fact reusable in relaxation/tuning analysis rather than a routine matrix exercise.
residual_risks: The exact crossover may not persist in this form for more than two rows.

final_claim: For a nonsingular real two-row cyclic Kaczmarz system with normalized row angle \(\theta\), \(s=\sin\theta\), and common relaxation \(0<\omega<2\), the one-sweep Euclidean operator norm is uniquely minimized by \(\omega=1\), while the asymptotic spectral-radius optimum \(\omega_\star=2/(1+s)\) is defective. Its exact \(k\)-sweep norm is \(q^k(\sqrt{1+4k^2s^2/c^2}+2ks/c)\) with \(q=(1-s)/(1+s)\), yielding the stated exact ratio to unrelaxed Kaczmarz and the near-parallel crossover scale \(k\asymp s^{-1/2}\) with critical scaled horizon \(\sqrt3/2\).
limitations: Exactly two independent real normalized rows and one common relaxation parameter are covered.
Performance is Euclidean solution-error norm after complete cyclic sweeps.
No corresponding formula is asserted for more rows, inconsistent systems, randomized order, row-dependent relaxation, or residual norms.
